title: Invalid mapping (generated column -1) when CSS contains <style and HTML escaping applies
publicBody:
Since 8.5.29, `SafeStringifier.escapeHTML` escapes `<style` / `<!--` in the output. When escaping kicks in, the source map generator adds a mapping with `generated.column: -1`, and `source-map-js` prints `Invalid mapping`.

### Reproduction

```js
import postcss from 'postcss'

const css = '/* see <style> */\na { color: red }\n'
const result = await postcss([{ postcssPlugin: 'noop', Once() {} }])
  .process(css, { from: 'in.css', map: { inline: false } })
console.log(result.css)
```

Output (postcss 8.5.29, Node 24):

```
Invalid mapping: {"generated":{"column":-1,"line":3},"source":"in.css","original":{"column":0,"line":3},"name":null}
/* see \3c style> */
a { color: red }
```

Without `<style` in the CSS there is no warning.

### Cause

In `lib/stringify.js`, if the escaped CSS differs from the original, the whole string is passed to the builder at once: `builder(escaped, node)` with the root node and no `type`. `MapGenerator.generateString` then treats it as both start and end of the root. For the end mapping it uses `column - 2`, and when the escaped string ends with `\n`, `column` is `1`, so the generated column becomes `-1`.

### Real-world impact

Vite 8 depends on `postcss@^8.5.29`, so any Vue SFC `<style>` block whose comment mentions `<style>` (for example `/* keep this in <style> */`) prints `Invalid mapping` in `nuxt dev` / `vite dev`.
